import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Drop rows with missing 'Income' values, as they are crucial for this analysis
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Calculate 'Total Spending' by summing all product-related columns
spending_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col.startswith('Mnt') and col.endswith('Prods')]
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Filter out extreme income values for better visualization clarity
# Based on typical customer datasets, incomes can have extreme outliers that skew plots.
# We'll filter to focus on the main distribution of customers.
# Assuming typical income ranges, values below 10000 or above 120000 might be outliers
# or represent a very small segment that distorts the overall view.
df_filtered = df[(df['Income'] > 10000) & (df['Income'] < 120000)].copy()

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='Income',
    y='TotalSpending',
    hue='Education',
    palette='viridis', # A color palette suitable for categorical data
    alpha=0.7,         # Transparency of points
    s=70,              # Size of points
    edgecolor='w',     # White edge around points for better separation
    linewidth=0.5      # Line width of the edge
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Total Spending vs. Income by Education Level', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Income ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending on Products ($)', fontsize=14)

# Improve legend placement
plt.legend(title='Education Level', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Customize x and y axis ticks for better readability
plt.ticklabel_format(style='plain', axis='x')
plt.ticklabel_format(style='plain', axis='y')
plt.xticks(fontsize=11)
plt.yticks(fontsize=11)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping and ensure everything fits
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
